config.title: SQLAlchemy & Alembic

intro.title: SQLAlchemy & Alembic
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Python application that connects to a database, defines a data model, and manages database schema changes. You'll learn how to use SQLAlchemy, a popular Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) library, to interact with databases using Python classes and objects. The lesson will also introduce Alembic, a tool for handling database migrations, which allows you to update your database schema safely as your application evolves. By the end, you'll understand how to set up a database connection, create models, and apply migrations to keep your database in sync with your code.
intro.usecase: SQLAlchemy and Alembic are essential for managing database operations in real-world Python applications like e-commerce platforms, content management systems, and financial dashboards. Developers use SQLAlchemy to build data models for user profiles, product catalogs, and transaction records, while Alembic handles schema migrations when adding new features like user authentication or payment processing. This combination ensures database changes are version-controlled and deployable without data loss, critical for maintaining live applications during updates.

objectives: Configure SQLAlchemy to establish a database connection with a Python application
Construct SQLAlchemy models to define database table structures
Initialize Alembic to manage database migrations for your project
Apply Alembic commands to generate and execute migration scripts
Manipulate database records using SQLAlchemy's session and query interfaces
Integrate SQLAlchemy models with Alembic migrations to evolve your database schema
Control database versioning by rolling back migrations when needed

steps.title: Query database records
steps.instruction: Create a new session, query all User records from the database, and print the results.
steps.hint: Use the SessionLocal factory to create a session, then use session.query(User).all() to get all records. Loop through the results and print each user's attributes.
steps.analogousExample:
# Example: Querying and printing records
session = SessionLocal()
users = session.query(User).all()
for user in users:
    print(f'User id: {user.id}, name: {user.name}')
steps.seedCode:

from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
# Add import for Session and sessionmaker here

# Your code will go below
engine = create_engine('sqlite:///example.db')
Base = declarative_base()

# Define the User model here
class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'users'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(String)

# Call create_all() to generate tables
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)

# Create session factory here
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(bind=engine)

steps.title: Initialize Alembic
steps.instruction: Initialize Alembic by calling the `init` command with the database URL and model metadata.
steps.hint: You can use the Alembic `init` command to set up the migration environment. Make sure to pass the database URL and model metadata as arguments.
steps.analogousExample:
# Example: Initialize Alembic
from alembic.config import Config
from alembic import command

# Initialize Alembic with database URL and model metadata
alembic_cfg = Config()
alembic_cfg.set_main_option('sqlalchemy.url', 'sqlite:///example.db')
command.init(alembic_cfg, 'migrations')
